tools.description: Report the authoritative inventory of metrics this platform declares, including declared-but-not-yet-computable metrics. Use it when the user asks what this platform can measure, report, or calculate; preserve any explicit source or storage context in source_reference. It is not needed to explain what a general advertising or retail concept means.

source_reference.description: Optional customer-facing source or storage context stated in a broad metric-discovery question. Pass it unchanged when present; the governed catalog either resolves the request or returns a natural limitation without substituting another source.

tools.name: catalog_list_metrics

tools.description: Report how this platform defines one declared metric: its governed formula, units, valid breakdowns, and caveats. Use it for claims about this platform's definition or support of a metric, not to explain general industry terminology, which needs no tool. Answers from the metric dictionary and reads no data.

grain.description: Optional exact dimension name to check for support. For every explicit 'by X', breakdown, or grain request, pass X unchanged even when it may be unsupported; never omit or substitute it to make the call succeed. Entity selection is separate, so mixed entity and grain wording must preserve both.

metric_name.description: A customer-facing metric reference: canonical name, label, or governed alias, for computable and declared-but-not-yet-computable metrics alike, resolved deterministically. An unresolvable or ambiguous reference returns a typed refusal naming alternatives rather than an approximation.

tools.name: catalog_describe_metric

tools.description: Resolve candidate semantic intent, then report one metric as a breakdown or trend over a closed period. Every candidate is resolved inside the server-configured, deployment-wide analytical scope before the existing measurement boundary executes.

currency_mode.description: Optional currency candidate: NATIVE or TARGET. NATIVE is the governed default. TARGET also requires target_currency; deterministic resolution accepts or refuses it with a typed reason.

entity_references.description: Optional map from a governed entity kind to customer-visible name text. Known kinds are ecosystem, platform, channel_group, channel, campaign, ad_product, marketplace, product, brand, and advertiser. A marketplace phrase such as 'United States marketplace' belongs under the marketplace key here as the customer-visible name only, for example 'United States'; omit the generic word 'marketplace' and never put the name under selectors. Pass every entity kind the customer names; deterministic resolution accepts what is supported and returns a typed refusal for what is not. Values must be names only; identifiers, keys, source scopes, and nested reference objects are refused. Audience segments are not an entity kind: they can't be named here, only broken down by with the audience_segment grain, and the answer names each segment.

grains.description: One or more customer-facing dimensions to break the figure down by, as semantic grain names, never storage columns. Retail and advertising: ad_product, campaign, channel, channel_group, date, ecosystem, marketplace, platform, product. Reach and funnel (shoppers_reached and the other exposure-group metrics): exposure_group and identity_space; frequency metrics: frequency_bucket. Audience segments (segment_impressions, segment_index and the other segment metrics): audience_segment, with campaign for one campaign's segments. Cohorts and repeat rates (repeat_buyer_rate and the other cohort metrics): cohort, acquisition_channel_group and months_since_acquisition. catalog_describe_metric lists the grains one metric supports.

max_rows.description: Optional. Ceiling on rows returned. The answer states when it was hit, so a truncated result is never mistaken for a complete one.

metric_reference.description: Customer-facing metric name, label, or governed alias to resolve deterministically. This is candidate intent, not an execution field; unknown or ambiguous text is refused. Customers and buyers are distinct people; purchases and orders are transactions, and one is never answered with the other. New-to-brand customers or buyers: buyers_new_to_brand_12mo, measured per complete week or month (time_grain week or month). New-to-brand purchases or orders: purchases_new_to_brand_12mo.

operation.description: Optional customer-facing operation candidate. Preserve explicit operation wording even when it may be unsupported; deterministic resolution returns the typed refusal. When omitted, the selected tool uses its own breakdown, comparison, or ranking default.

period_end_candidate.description: Optional candidate last day, inclusive, as YYYY-MM-DD. It requires period_start_candidate and cannot include the open current day.

period_reference.description: Optional exact governed period name, such as 'the 7 days ending yesterday'. Supply this or both candidate period dates, never both modes. When the question names no period at all, omit every period argument: the platform answers for the latest published coverage and the answer discloses the window it chose.

period_start_candidate.description: Optional candidate first day, inclusive, as YYYY-MM-DD. It becomes authoritative only after deterministic closed-period resolution and requires period_end_candidate.

report_lenses.description: Optional map of customer-requested report-lens names to values. Every name and value is resolved through the governed vocabulary; omitted applicable lenses use governed defaults.

selectors.description: Optional map of exact semantic selector names to governed values. Supply only selectors required by the chosen metric (catalog_describe_metric lists them); values are resolved exactly, and a selector the metric allows only one value for is pinned for you. time_grain is the kind of period the question asks about: week for a Monday to Sunday week, month for a calendar month (such as September, or last month), quarter for a calendar quarter, custom for a cohort metric's vintage. profile_path says whose segment profile is read: asi_in_market or asi_lifestyle for the shoppers your ads reached, profiled with Amazon audience segments (paid); dsp_exposed_only for DSP-exposed buyers, with DSP behaviour segments. The paths are never combined, so when the question doesn't say which, ask. cohort_path: standard for ad-touched repeat purchases, arp for all Amazon purchases. Marketplace, product, campaign, channel, and other entity names belong in entity_references, never in this map.

source_dataset_selector.description: Optional candidate source-dataset name paired with source_system_selector. Pass explicit source wording unchanged; deterministic resolution accepts or refuses it with a typed reason. No caller source scope or source identifier is accepted.

source_system_selector.description: Optional candidate source-system name paired with source_dataset_selector. Pass explicit source wording unchanged; deterministic resolution accepts or refuses it with a typed reason.

target_currency.description: Optional three-letter target currency candidate, used only with currency_mode TARGET.
